findings.F1: The main measure is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: the mean excess 5-day return on positive-forecast grid bars is +0.37 % with t 1.72 over 2457 cases, and the positive-forecast cases beat the flat cases (excess −0.40 %, t −1.74, 2275 cases) by a Welch t of 2.45.
findings.F2: The effect is weak and spread thinly rather than concentrated in one part of the data. 12 of 15 coins have a positive mean excess, but none has a t above 1.24 (LTC +0.77 %, t 1.24; XRP +0.88 %, t 1.00). Only 50 % of the 24 windows have a positive mean.
findings.F3: The effect changes sign across years rather than holding in one regime. It is positive in 2020 (+1.35 %, t 1.92), 2021 (+1.76 %, t 1.91) and 2024 (+0.91 %, t 2.17), and negative in 2018 (−1.84 %, t −1.63) and 2022 (−1.32 %, t −2.07). The market's own moves drown it out.
findings.F4: The grading holds only loosely, so the strongest forecasts do not isolate a clearer effect. The lowest quarter of positive forecasts earns −0.11 % (t −0.26), q2 +0.67 %, q3 +0.17 % and the top quarter +0.76 % (t 1.72). The larger-minus-smaller-half check is +0.19 %.

ideas.name: nearness reversal, all coins
ideas.idea: For a coin's nearness to its 90-day high, the higher that signal's predictive power for the coin's 5-day returns over the past 365 days, the lower the same signal's predictive power over the following 90 days. The turn shows on the rising side: the more strongly this reversal points up, the higher the coin's return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should act on the turnaround of a nearness-to-high relation only by buying, in proportion to the reversal's strength, and refuse the shorts that lost the book 41 % in a rally.
